title: Occupational Health and Safety Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Software vendors and service organisations that compete for the same customers and jobs as Kitry, the Belgian occupational health and safety SaaS vendor modeled in this domain: large employers in France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands that run their own (internal or autonomous) occupational health service, an HSE/prevention function and an HR department, and need medical surveillance planning, a confidential occupational medical file, risk assessment and action plans, accident and occupational disease declarations, employee and manager portals and regulatory reporting on one HDS/ISO 27001-hosted platform. Kitry is included as the modeled company so that the other players' figures can be read against its own.
inclusionLogic: global EHS suites (Cority, Enablon, Intelex, VelocityEHS, Sphera, EcoOnline, Quentic, Benchmark Gensuite) that a multinational's group headquarters may standardise on for safety, incidents, chemicals, compliance and ESG, and that increasingly bundle an occupational health module; they compete for Kitry's workplace safety, accident, chemical and analytics modules and, in Cority's case, for the medical file itself

health-first occupational health specialists in France (padoa, Val Solutions) that already run the medical file, convocations, questionnaires, devices and portals for inter-company services (SPSTI) and autonomous enterprise services, i.e. the head-to-head alternatives in a French internal-service selection and the most likely entrants into Benelux
regulatory compliance SaaS (Preventeo) that substitutes for the risk-assessment, chemical-inventory and compliance-proof bricks at French industrial groups without touching medical surveillance

external prevention services (IDEWE, representative of Belgian SEPP/EDPB such as Mensura and of French SPSTI) that a Benelux employer can choose instead of running an internal service on Kitry; they come with their own client software and therefore compete for the buyer rather than for the licence, so they are listed as substitutes

geographic focus on Benelux and France, the markets in which Kitry sells and in which country-specific content (DMST, DUERP, CERFA, Fedris, Belgian prevention plans) decides selections; global suites are included because they are the group-HQ alternative, not because they hold local regulatory content
notes: Business stats are only included when they were found on official company websites, product and about pages, official newsrooms and press releases, official investor or parent-company pages, or press-wire distributions issued by the company itself (Cority via GlobeNewswire; Wolters Kluwer via GlobeNewswire and its own results PDF); each stat preserves the company's reported scope and period, and players for which no official figure could be verified carry only the figures that could be.

Vendors report at very different scopes: Wolters Kluwer publishes group and division revenue that says nothing about Enablon alone (only the EHS & ESG growth rate and its 31% share of the division); Sphera, VelocityEHS, Intelex, EcoOnline and Benchmark Gensuite publish company-wide customer, user or worker counts across all product lines; padoa and Val Solutions count workers covered on their platforms; Kitry reports employee records, active users, customer organisations and medical files; IDEWE reports employers and workers served as a service organisation. 'Users' (named logins), 'workers covered' (employees whose files exist), 'employee records' and 'medical files' are not interchangeable, and none of these figures is directly comparable with Kitry's 150+ organisations, 6,000+ users, 4M+ employee records and 2.5M+ medical files.

Several players sit inside larger groups (Enablon inside Wolters Kluwer's Corporate Performance & ESG division; Intelex inside Fortive via Industrial Scientific; Quentic inside AMCS; Sphera owned by Blackstone; VelocityEHS backed by CVC Growth and Partners Group; EcoOnline backed by Apax; Val Solutions owned by Extens; padoa backed by Kamet Ventures and Five Arrows); group-level figures are labeled with that scope.

Kitry does not publish revenue or headcount; its figures come from kitry.com (35+ years, 4M+ employee records, 6,000+ active users, 50%+ self-service adoption, HDS and ISO 27001) and from Vortex Capital Partners' investment page and 29 March 2022 release (150+ customers, 2.5M+ medical files, 100+ customers at the time of the deal). Some Kitry marketing pages cite 4.5 million medical records; the lower Vortex figure is retained here.

padoa's EUR 80 million equity-and-debt round of February 2022 led by Five Arrows Growth Capital was reported by trade press and by the advising law firm but no padoa-owned page describing it could be retrieved, so it is mentioned only in the description and not recorded as a business stat.

Vendors checked but excluded: Mensura and other Belgian external services (IDEWE is listed as the representative substitute), Meddbase (now part of Cority), Alcumus (EHS software now part of EcoOnline), HRIS suites such as SAP SuccessFactors and Workday (data sources, not occupational health systems), and clinical EHR vendors (out of the domain boundary).

players.name: Kitry (modeled company)
players.hq: Nivelles, Belgium (group base reported as Antwerp in the 2022 Vortex release)
players.description: Kitry is the modeled subject of this domain: a Belgian vendor with 35+ years of occupational health and safety software expertise that sells a modular, multilingual (FR/NL/EN) SaaS platform covering occupational health, workplace safety, work accidents and occupational diseases, employee and manager portals and cross-module KPIs, hosted on HDS- and ISO 27001-certified infrastructure, together with a services arm that assesses, configures, migrates, trains and supports every customer. It serves large organisations in France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands (SNCF, Thales, Ville de Paris, Ville de Bruxelles, Umicore, Empreva, Engie, BNP, EIB, Stellantis, EDF, RATP, CNRS, Disney, BASF) and has been backed by Vortex Capital Partners since a strategic partnership announced on 29 March 2022 that funds the 'Kitry as a Service' pure-play SaaS transition. It is listed so the other players' figures can be read against its own.

players.name: Cority
players.description: Cority is the global EHS and sustainability suite whose roots are in occupational health: its CorityOne platform bundles a Health Cloud (occupational health, clinical case management, medical surveillance, industrial hygiene) with safety, environmental, quality and sustainability clouds, and it reinforced the health side in January 2025 by acquiring Meddbase, a UK cloud-native occupational medicine and practice-management vendor. Cority states that it was named a Leader for the sixth time in Verdantix's Green Quadrant EHS Software 2025 report, with the highest industrial hygiene score and standout occupational health results. For a Kitry prospect it is the enterprise-grade, English-first alternative when a multinational's group HQ standardises occupational health on one global suite rather than a Benelux/France specialist.

players.name: Intelex (Fortive)
players.description: Intelex, founded in 1992 and describing itself as the oldest independent EHS and quality software vendor in North America, sells a configurable EHSQ platform (safety, incident, audit, environmental, quality and health modules) that has been part of Fortive since Industrial Scientific acquired it from JMI Equity and HarbourVest in 2019. With offices in Toronto, Denver, Reading (UK) and Singapore, it reaches European multinationals through the group HQ and competes with Kitry mainly on the safety, incident and compliance side and on the platform-configurability promise, while its occupational health depth is thinner than a health-first specialist.

players.name: Quentic (AMCS Group)
players.description: Quentic, founded in Berlin in 2007, is the leading German-speaking EHSQ and ESG SaaS vendor, with ten integrated modules (health and safety, risks and audits, incidents, hazardous chemicals, legal compliance, online instructions, processes, environmental management, sustainability and control) and subsidiaries across eleven European countries including Belgium, the Netherlands and France. players.name: padoa
players.description: padoa is the venture-built French occupational health platform (founded 2016 inside Kamet Ventures) that digitised the inter-company prevention services (SPSTI) with an appointment engine, pre-visit questionnaires, connected devices, teleconsultation, the Noa risk-assessment tool for employers and an employee app, on HDS, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified hosting. It reported an EUR 80 million equity-and-debt round led by Five Arrows Growth Capital in February 2022 and now states 9 million employees monitored, 350 staff and a German subsidiary. It is Kitry's most direct French rival: it dominates the SPSTI channel and sells to autonomous enterprise services too, so any French internal occupational health service compares the two, and its European expansion aims at the same Benelux ground.
